title: Don Beyer Wins Democratic Primary in Virginia’s 8th District
dek: Rep. Don Beyer won the Democratic primary for Virginia’s 8th Congressional District with 39,714 votes, or 67.6 percent of the total, according to the reported results.
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Lead image for Don Beyer Wins Democratic Primary in Virginia’s 8th District
hero.caption: Don Beyer Wins Democratic Primary in Virginia’s 8th District. Image from Falls Church News-Press.

body: Rep. Don Beyer won the Democratic primary for Virginia’s 8th Congressional District with 39,714 votes, or 67.6 percent of the total, according to the reported results.
Mo Seifeldein finished second with 17 percent, followed by Adam Dunigan with 9 percent. Overall turnout in the district was 9 percent.

title: Fairfax County apartment rents slip modestly, with Tysons median at $2,666
dek: Apartment rents across Fairfax County declined modestly in July, extending a period of soft conditions that analysts have linked partly to elevated multifamily construction.
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Lease now sign for the Edmund Apartments at Halley Rise in Reston in winter
hero.caption: Lease now sign for the Edmund Apartments at Halley Rise in Reston in winter (staff photo by Angela Woolsey)

body: Apartment rents across Fairfax County declined modestly in July, extending a period of soft conditions that analysts have linked partly to elevated multifamily construction.

The county’s median rent for all apartment sizes was $2,430 in July 2026, down from $2,463 a year earlier, a 1.3% decline. Median rents were $2,082 for one-bedroom units and $2,412 for two-bedroom units.

body: Fairfax County is seeking public- and private-sector ideas for updating its trash and recycling operations, a planning effort that could shape near-term improvements and longer-term decisions about the county’s solid-waste system.

The Department of Public Works and Environmental Services issued a request for expressions of interest Aug. 4. Submissions are being accepted through Oct. 30. The request is not an official bid, and it does not establish a future change to residential collection service.

title: Falls Church-raised science-fiction author Ted White dies at 88
dek: Theodore Edwin “Ted” White, a science-fiction author and editor raised in Falls Church, died May 24, 2026, at age 88, according to a death confirmation cited by PulpFest and the Science...
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Lead image for Falls Church-raised science-fiction author Ted White dies at 88
hero.caption: Falls Church-raised science-fiction author Ted White dies at 88. Image from Falls Church News-Press.

body: Theodore Edwin “Ted” White, a science-fiction author and editor raised in Falls Church, died May 24, 2026, at age 88, according to a death confirmation cited by PulpFest and the Science Fiction Encyclopedia. The synthesis reports that White experienced health problems after a fall at his home; that account should be independently verified.

White later worked as a copy editor for the Falls Church News-Press. His career in science fiction included writing or co-writing numerous novels and stories, sometimes under the pseudonyms Ron Archer and Norman Edwards.

title: Reston penthouse sells for $10.9 million, setting Virginia condominium record
dek: A full-floor penthouse at JW Marriott Residences Reston Station sold for $10.9 million, setting a Virginia record for a condominium sale, according to the development’s owner and the...
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.caption: The digital crown sign for JW Marriott at Reston Station (staff photo by Angela Woolsey)

body: A full-floor penthouse at JW Marriott Residences Reston Station sold for $10.9 million, setting a Virginia record for a condominium sale, according to the development’s owner and the brokerage that led the transaction.

The residence occupies the building’s 28th floor. Its sale surpassed the previous Virginia condominium sale-price record: a $10.25 million transaction at JW Marriott Residences Reston Station in April 2026.

title: VDOT proposes $8.7 million reconstruction of Popes Head Road curve

author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.caption: A car passes by the intersection of Popes Head Road (Route 654) and Quiet Brook Road (Route 7447) on a recent August afternoon. (staff photo by Mary Stachyra Lopez)

body: The Virginia Department of Transportation is proposing an $8.7 million reconstruction of a section of Popes Head Road near Fairfax Station, saying the work could improve safety at an S-curve between Quiet Brook Road and Revercomb Court.

VDOT presented the conceptual plan during a July 28 public information meeting. The proposal covers about one-fifth of a mile of Route 654 and would straighten the curve, improve sight distance and upgrade drainage with stormwater management systems.

title: Virginia sales tax holiday returns Aug. 7–9

author: Tysons Times Staff

body: Virginia’s three-day sales tax holiday will run from Friday, Aug. 7, through Sunday, Aug. 9, giving shoppers a temporary exemption on qualifying school supplies, clothing, footwear, emergency-preparedness items and certain Energy Star and WaterSense products.
The holiday begins at 12:01 a.m. Friday and ends at 11:59 p.m. Sunday. The exemption applies to qualifying purchases made in stores and online.

title: Beyer, Mizusawa and Beckwith win Fairfax primary contests
dek: Fairfax County voters chose nominees in Democratic and Republican congressional and U.S. Senate primaries Aug. 4, setting up three Nov. 3 general-election contests while reported results...
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Voting at Lake Braddock Secondary School
hero.caption: Voting at Lake Braddock Secondary School (staff photo by Jared Serre)
hero.credit: Voting at Lake Braddock Secondary School (staff photo by Jared Serre)

body: Fairfax County voters chose nominees in Democratic and Republican congressional and U.S. Senate primaries Aug. 4, setting up three Nov. 3 general-election contests while reported results remain unofficial pending certification.

Don Beyer won the Democratic nomination in Virginia’s 8th Congressional District and will face Republican Tony Sabio in November. Bert Mizusawa won the Republican U.S. Senate nomination and will face incumbent Sen. Mark Warner. Dave Beckwith won the Republican nomination in the 10th Congressional District and will face incumbent Rep. Suhas Subramanyam.

title: Faces of ONE campaign to spotlight Richmond Highway businesses amid redevelopment

hero.credit: Richmond Highway (staff photo by James Jarvis)

body: The Southeast Fairfax Development Corporation is expanding its Faces of ONE public art and placemaking initiative into a marketing campaign for Richmond Highway businesses and the broader corridor.

SFDC plans to introduce the expanded initiative to the public and local businesses on Aug. 13, 2026. The campaign includes small-business and corridor marketing, a new website, and locally produced photography and videography. SFDC also plans to spend more than $100,000 on digital advertising over the next year, according to the campaign’s current plan.

body: Virginia health officials are investigating the state’s first documented locally acquired dengue virus infection, a case they say is epidemiologically linked to an internationally acquired infection involving a Loudoun County resident.

The investigation was announced Aug. 4 by the Virginia Department of Health. It involves VDH, the Fairfax County Health Department and the Loudoun County Health Department. One dengue patient lives in Fairfax County and the other lives in Loudoun County.

body: Vienna is expected to receive its first five Capital Bikeshare stations by mid-August, bringing 21 standard bicycles and four electric bicycles to locations around town and linking Vienna to the regional bikeshare network.

The planned stations are near the W&OD Trail and Navy Federal Credit Union; at the Vienna Community Center, 120 Cherry Street SE; at Maple Avenue and Nutley Street; at 444 Maple Avenue W; and on Patrick Street SE near Park Street.

body: EYA Development is seeking Fairfax County approval to redevelop approximately 49 acres of Lake Fairfax Business Park in Reston with 1,017 homes and 27,900 square feet of retail and amenity space.

The two-phase proposal would rezone part of the 88-acre property at 1780 Business Center Drive from industrial use to planned residential mixed-use development. The site is near the Wiehle-Reston East Metro station.

body: Fairfax City Council members expressed mixed views July 28 about a preliminary proposal to redevelop a 2.09-acre office parcel at 3541 Chain Bridge Road.

Network Realty Partners is considering replacing two 1970s-era, two-story office buildings at the southeast corner of Chain Bridge Road and Eaton Place with 37 residential units, 2,750 square feet of retail space and proposed green space or a linear park.

title: Fairfax County unemployment reaches 3.6% as jobless count rises 10%
dek: Fairfax County’s unemployment rate rose to 3.6% in June, up from 3.2% a year earlier, according to preliminary data reported by the Virginia Department of Workforce Development and...
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Virginia Career Works advertises job transition resources on a Metro train
hero.caption: Virginia Career Works advertises job transition resources on a Metro train (staff photo by Angela Woolsey)

body: Fairfax County’s unemployment rate rose to 3.6% in June, up from 3.2% a year earlier, according to preliminary data reported by the Virginia Department of Workforce Development and Advancement and the federal Bureau of Labor Statistics.
The county had 22,888 residents counted as unemployed in June 2026. That was a 10% increase from the number reported a year earlier, according to the comparison published by FFXnow on Aug. 4.

title: Fairfax County’s office-to-housing push reaches Reston, Herndon and Vienna

author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Exterior of a largely vacant multistory office building
hero.caption: Vacant and underused office properties are increasingly being considered for housing redevelopment.

body: Fairfax County and nearby municipalities are pursuing redevelopment of vacant or aging office and commercial properties into housing and mixed-use communities, with proposals spanning Reston, Herndon and Vienna.

The effort includes the 119-acre Reston East Planning Study, which covers land north of Sunrise Valley Drive between Upper Lake Drive and Hunter Mill Road. Supervisor Walter Alcorn initiated the study in April, and the county held or publicized an open house on Aug. 4.

title: Northern Virginia experts urge vigilance as drowning can happen silently

author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Lifeguard watching swimmers from an elevated chair
hero.caption: Water-safety experts stress close supervision because drowning can happen quickly and quietly.

body: Drowning can happen quietly and in under 30 seconds, according to a water-safety feature published Aug. 4 by Connection Newspapers that highlights prevention and emergency response guidance from Northern Virginia professionals.
Dr. Miriam Fischer, a MedStar Health emergency physician who previously worked in the Emergency Department at Inova Fairfax Hospital, said drowning often does not look the way bystanders expect.

title: Northern Virginia remains under drought warning as officials urge conservation
dek: Northern Virginia remains under a drought warning advisory, with officials urging residents to reduce outdoor watering and other nonessential water use.
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Dry, cracked lakebed during a prolonged drought
hero.caption: Dry lakebed conditions illustrate the effects of a prolonged rainfall deficit and drought.

body: Northern Virginia remains under a drought warning advisory, with officials urging residents to reduce outdoor watering and other nonessential water use.

The advisory covers Arlington, Fairfax, Fauquier, Loudoun and Prince William counties, along with several independent cities. Virginia’s Drought Monitoring Task Force continued the warning July 31 after reviewing precipitation, streamflow, groundwater, reservoirs, soil moisture, agricultural conditions, water-supply impacts and the U.S. Drought Monitor.

title: Opposition mounts over proposed Edsall Road substation for Plaza 500 data center

body: Opposition is mounting to Dominion Energy’s proposal for a 176-megawatt substation and associated 230-kilovolt transmission line intended to serve Starwood Capital Group’s planned Plaza 500 South data center in Lincolnia.

The Fairfax County application, numbered 2232-2025-MA-00007, would connect the proposed Edsall Road substation with the existing Van Dorn substation. The substation remains under county review, while the State Corporation Commission has approved the transmission lines between the two substations.

The leased space covers the building’s entire 11th, 12th and 13th floors. QTS plans to use the Reston Row location for headquarters administrative functions supporting the company’s growth.

title: Former Virginia Sen. Janet Howell, longtime Tysons-area representative, dies at 82
dek: Former Virginia state Sen. Janet Howell, who represented Tysons and neighboring Fairfax and Arlington communities for more than three decades, has died at 82, according to reports...
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.caption: Former Virginia Sen. Janet Howell, longtime Tysons-area representative, dies at 82. Image from WTOP Fairfax County.

body: Former Virginia state Sen. Janet Howell, who represented Tysons and neighboring Fairfax and Arlington communities for more than three decades, has died at 82, according to reports published Aug. 3.

Howell served in the Virginia Senate from 1992 until her retirement in 2024. She represented the 32nd Senate District, which included Tysons, Reston, Wolf Trap, northern Chantilly, portions of McLean and parts of Arlington County.

body: Founding Farmers is seeking Fairfax County approval to operate small on-site distilleries at its existing restaurants in Tysons and Reston.

The proposed distilleries would be located at 1800 Tysons Blvd. in Tysons and 1904 Reston Metro Plaza in Reston. Each would produce no more than 5,000 gallons of spirits per year for restaurant patrons.

title: McLean Leads Bright MLS Region in Luxury-Home Sales During Q2

body: McLean’s 22101 ZIP code recorded the highest number of luxury-home sales in the Bright MLS service region during the second quarter of 2026, according to Bright MLS data.
The ZIP code recorded 76 luxury sales out of 144 total sales from April 1 through June 30. Vienna’s 22180 ZIP code ranked fifth, with 42 luxury sales out of 107 total sales.

author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.caption: Paul Thomas was nominated to be the new Hunter Mill District planning commissioner (courtesy of Paul Thomas)

body: Walter Alcorn plans to recommend lifelong Restonian Paul Thomas as the Fairfax County Planning Commission representative for Hunter Mill District, following John Carter’s announcement that he will retire after nearly nine years in the role.

The Fairfax County Board of Supervisors was scheduled to consider Thomas’s nomination on Aug. 25, 2026. The nomination had not yet been approved at publication. If approved, Thomas was expected to begin serving Sept. 1.

title: Revised Courthouse Plaza plan draws generally favorable, qualified council response
dek: Combined Properties presented revised conceptual plans for a two-phase redevelopment of Fairfax City’s approximately 10-acre Courthouse Plaza site during a July 28 City Council work...
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Rendering of a modern multi-story apartment building with red brick and beige facades, lined by trees along a street.
hero.caption: Revamped conceptual design of housing on Courthouse Plaza parcel (via Combined Properties)

body: Combined Properties presented revised conceptual plans for a two-phase redevelopment of Fairfax City’s approximately 10-acre Courthouse Plaza site during a July 28 City Council work session, drawing generally favorable reactions from council members while leaving questions about the number of new homes.

The proposal remains under consideration and was not presented as an approved development. If it advances, the plan would add 630 multifamily residential units in buildings up to six stories, along with approximately 62,000 square feet of retail, more than 1,700 parking spaces and approximately 120,000 square feet of open space.

title: TJ Students Build Tool to Track School Board Decisions
dek: Students at Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology have launched Civic Cycle, a free web application designed to help residents follow local school board meetings.
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Fairfax County Public School buses
hero.caption: Fairfax County Public School buses idle at a middle school in Falls Church, Va., July 20, 2020. (AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)

body: Students at Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology have launched Civic Cycle, a free web application designed to help residents follow local school board meetings.

The tool imports school board agendas from BoardDocs and detects when a new meeting is published. It then uses Claude AI to generate a meeting summary. The student group says every AI-generated summary is reviewed by a human before it is published.

title: Serverfarm seeks zoning exceptions for proposed Tysons data center
dek: Serverfarm is seeking Fairfax County zoning exceptions to convert two existing office buildings and a parking garage at 7980 and 7990 Quantum Drive into a 316,000-square-foot data center...

hero.caption: Overlooking a hedge into a parking lot, with a shopping mall and a skyscraper in the background in Tysons, Virginia. (WTOP/Scott Gelman)

body: Serverfarm is seeking Fairfax County zoning exceptions to convert two existing office buildings and a parking garage at 7980 and 7990 Quantum Drive into a 316,000-square-foot data center called Vienna Cloud.

The proposal comes as Fairfax County applies stricter data-center standards adopted in 2024. The project does not meet several of those requirements, including rules concerning proximity to Metro stations, building area and buffers near residential neighborhoods.

title: 49-home subdivision proposed on Pohick Episcopal Church property in Lorton
dek: Pohick Episcopal Church and Christopher Land LLC have submitted a Fairfax County rezoning application for Cunningham Woods Reserve, a proposed 49-home subdivision on approximately 17.5...

body: Pohick Episcopal Church and Christopher Land LLC have submitted a Fairfax County rezoning application for Cunningham Woods Reserve, a proposed 49-home subdivision on approximately 17.5 acres of the church’s historic property in Lorton.

The application, submitted to the county planning department July 16, 2026, seeks to rezone the western portion of the 43-acre church parcel at 9301 Richmond Highway, near Pohick Road and Telegraph Road. The property is currently zoned R-1 and operates under a special-use permit. The applicants are requesting a change to PDH-3 zoning, which would allow greater development intensity.

body: Charles Schwab plans to open a financial-services branch in the former Four Sisters restaurant space in Merrifield’s Mosaic District.
The branch is planned for 8190 Strawberry Lane, Suite 1. Charles Schwab has not announced when it will open.

title: Renovation of Centreville High stalled as families press for fixes
dek: Centreville High School families are pushing Fairfax County officials to address reported building deficiencies while a voter-approved renovation project sits on hold, caught between a...
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: A temporary trailer at Centreville High School in Fairfax County, Virginia.
hero.caption: A temporary trailer at Centreville High School in Fairfax County, Virginia.
hero.credit: A temporary trailer at Centreville High School in Fairfax County, Virginia.

body: Centreville High School families are pushing Fairfax County officials to address reported building deficiencies while a voter-approved renovation project sits on hold, caught between a zoning dispute and the district's reassessment of whether the school still needs added capacity.

Voters approved funding for the renovation and expansion in 2021, and the district submitted building permits in January 2025. But architectural and engineering design work has been paused pending resolution of a Floor Area Ratio zoning issue that affects the site plan. Resolving the problem may require discussions with the Fairfax County Park Authority and possibly the Board of Supervisors.

title: Wolf Trap plans November debut for relocated Virginian Barn
dek: Wolf Trap plans to begin operating the relocated and renovated Virginian Barn in November, adding a third historic structure to The Barns at Wolf Trap.
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Modern glass-fronted barn-like building with wooden siding, illuminated at dusk among trees and lawn for a serene landscape scene;
hero.caption: The Barns at Wolf Trap will open The Virginian Barn as a dining and gathering space in November. (courtesy of Wolf Trap Foundation for the Performing Arts)

body: Wolf Trap plans to begin operating the relocated and renovated Virginian Barn in November, adding a third historic structure to The Barns at Wolf Trap.

The 2,500-square-foot barn, built in the early 1900s, was disassembled and moved from its longtime home in Loudoun County to Wolf Trap earlier in 2026. The renovated building will provide space for dining, gatherings, special events and private rentals. Kitchen and restroom facilities have also been added inside.

title: Arts partnership marks five seasons of opening Capital One Hall to local groups

body: ArtsFairfax, Capital One and local artists marked five seasons of a partnership designed to make Capital One Hall more accessible to Fairfax County arts and culture nonprofits at a July 14 reception in Tysons.

Program officials reported that 48 participating nonprofits collectively attracted more than 61,000 attendees and generated $2.4 million in ticket revenue over those seasons. The totals were presented by the program and were not independently substantiated in the supplied reporting.

title: ‘Tysons 150’ documentary looks back at growth — and ahead to unresolved challenges

body: Fairfax County Channel 16 scheduled the first screening of “Tysons 150,” a 42-minute documentary about the community’s transformation, for 7 p.m. July 29 at LOOK Dine-In Cinemas in The Boro.

The film is part of “Providence Perspectives,” Channel 16’s oral-history series. The free public event at 1667 Silver Hill Drive was also set to include a 6 p.m. happy hour, with advance registration encouraged. Because the available source was published before the screening, it does not establish whether the premiere occurred as planned.

title: Fairfax Teens' Finance Book for Kids Goes Global

hero.credit: Oakton High School students hold their new book on financial literacy for eleme…

body: Three Oakton High School students turned a school project into an international effort to teach young children about money management through storytelling.

Dev Rai, Austin Chen, and Ayush Ranjan created "The Seed That Grows," a children's book designed to introduce elementary students to concepts like saving, investing, and delayed gratification. The Fairfax County teens wrote the story and created all the illustrations themselves as part of a DECA financial literacy initiative.

title: Oakton students turn financial lessons into a book for younger readers

author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.alt: Oakton High School students hold their new book on financial literacy

body: Three Oakton High School students are using a simple choice between planting a seed and trading it for candy to introduce elementary school pupils to personal finance.

Dev Rai, Austin Chen and Ayush Ranjan wrote and illustrated “The Seed That Grows” as part of a DECA financial-literacy initiative. Their story uses the growth of a seed to explain saving, investing and the value of waiting for a larger reward.

title: Arlington's Gift of Bells: A Tower That Rang Through Generations
dek: The rope hung rough and hairy from the tower at James Whitcomb Riley Elementary School, and every morning Mr. Brown the custodian gave it a pull. That clang sent a clear message across...
author: Tysons Times Staff

hero.caption: "Thinking about that old bell made me remember other sonorous bells I’ve heard in my life...." Netherlands Carillon at U.S. Marine Corps War Memorial, Marshall Dr., Arlington. Courtesy Washington DC Cherry Blossom Watch.

body: The rope hung rough and hairy from the tower at James Whitcomb Riley Elementary School, and every morning Mr. Brown the custodian gave it a pull. That clang sent a clear message across the neighborhood: walk faster, pedal harder, or face the shame of a tardy slip.
For one student who loved school, the bell meant something different. It was a daily invitation, a sound that promised another day of learning was about to begin.

body: Summer isn't over yet. With back-to-school season approaching, August packs in a final burst of outdoor entertainment across Northern Virginia and the surrounding region, from agricultural fairs showcasing livestock and tractor demos to festivals celebrating oysters, bourbon, and watermelons.

The Fairfax County Summer Carnival and Fair kicks off July 30 through August 2 at Frying Pan Farm Park in Herndon. Families can expect carnival rides, farm animals, tractor demonstrations, and fair food. Big Truck Night runs Friday, July 31, from 5 to 7 p.m. Parking costs $10 Friday through Sunday.

body: When the curtain rises tonight at South Lakes High School in Reston, students from 11 Fairfax County schools will share the stage with adult actors in a groundbreaking collaboration that's reshaping summer theater in the region.

The production of "Dear Evan Hansen" marks the first joint venture between Fairfax County Public Schools students and the Reston Community Players, creating what organizers describe as a mentorship program that pairs young performers with experienced community theater veterans.

body: Soccer camps may be overflowing this summer, but a different kind of training is underway at Oak Hill Elementary School in Herndon—one that could shape how Fairfax County students handle their wallets for life.

Money Camp immerses students in Cent City, a miniature economy where they apply for jobs, open bank accounts, launch businesses, and sell their own products by week's end. The five-day program gives elementary schoolers a compressed taste of financial adulthood.

Inside a simulated town called Cent City, campers applied for jobs, managed bank accounts and launched businesses. Along the way, they encountered taxes, insurance costs and the decisions involved in turning an idea into a product that customers might buy.

body: A LEGO display celebrating Fairfax County’s 250th anniversary is now on view at Tysons Corner Center, bringing landmarks and everyday scenes from all nine magisterial districts into one installation.

The Northern Virginia Lego User Group, also known as NOVA-LUG, unveiled the display July 22 near the mall’s future Dick’s House of Sport store. The project is part of Fairfax County programming commemorating the United States’ 250th anniversary and is expected to remain at Tysons Corner Center into January 2027.

body: The Falls Church Kiwanis Little League 12U Majors All-Stars advanced to the Virginia state semifinals after a four-game winning streak, extending a historic tournament run that began with the 2026 District 4 championship.

Falls Church opened state pool play July 17 with a 13-1 victory over Bedford Metro. James Labukas, Hunter Roy and Will Talbert each recorded multiple hits as the team began the tournament with a decisive win.

body: The baseball facility at Westfield High School will be named the Rob Hahne Memorial Baseball Field, honoring a longtime coach whose work extended across youth sports and charitable organizations in Northern Virginia.

The Fairfax County School Board approved the name at approximately 1:30 a.m. July 17 during a lengthy meeting. The measure passed through the board’s consent agenda, and members did not discuss it publicly during the meeting.

body: The Falls Church Kiwanis Little League 12U Majors All Stars Team delivered a summer that will echo through the community for years to come, capturing a District 4 championship and advancing further in the state tournament than any team in the league's history.

The squad's remarkable run began June 1 and culminated at the state tournament last week, where they tore through pool play with a 13-1 victory over Bedford Metro and a 15-1 rout of Roanoke City. Colin Dailey and Spencer Allan combined for eight strikeouts in the Roanoke win, setting the tone for what was to come.

body: The World Cup final between Spain and Argentina descended into chaos, brawling, and 46 combined fouls—exposing deep flaws in soccer's antiquated rulebook that FIFA stubbornly refuses to modernize.

Five billion viewers tuned into this summer's tournament, hosted across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, generating over $15 billion in revenue. Yet the July 19 championship match gave the world an ugly showcase of everything wrong with the Beautiful Game's governance.

body: Danny Jolles may live in Los Angeles, but his sports allegiance remains firmly planted in the Washington region.

The comedian and actor, known for roles in “Hacks” and “Crazy Ex-Girlfriend” and appearances on “The Late Show with Stephen Colbert,” proudly represents the Commanders from the West Coast. His commitment extends far beyond football: If a team carries Washington, D.C., in its name, Jolles considers it his team — including the UFL’s D.C. Defenders.
